messages:
lina: heads-up: seeing a p99 spike and a handful of IO errors on ephemeral nvme nodes in us-west-2. Affected hosts are running transient batch jobs. not the usual scrub pattern, looks like lots of small random writes + deletes. dmesg shows occasional blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...

mike: can you paste a short iostat or iotop when it happens? also any recent kernel/firmware changes?

lina: here's a quick snip from right now:
```
$ sudo iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s   rrqm/s  wrqm/s  %util
nvme0n1         12.5   340.2   1024.0  81920.0    0.00    5.00  97.80
```
and a short dmesg around the error:
```
[234567.123456] nvme0n1: completions qid 6 failed status 0x5
[234567.123461] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 18446744073709551615
```
not firmware-update-y; this started after we rolled the new batch job that shards checkpoint files aggressively.

arya: maybe the job is creating a ton of sparse files then punching holes? sparse writes + immediate unlink can cause weird write amplification on some controllers (esp with compression). Any fio pattern test we can run that mimics it?

lina: good idea. i ran a quick fio mimic on one node (small-file random write + delete):
```
fio --name=randrw --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=8 --iodepth=32 --runtime=60
```
results looked similar: very high %util and high latency tail.

mike: can we triage if it's the controller or the kernel path? try toggling io scheduler / enabling/disabling writeback cache? if this is on k8s, maybe kubelet's ephemeral-cleaner is racing deletes. Which eviction/cleanup service is deleting checkpoints?

lina: ephemeral-cleaner (our cronjob that nukes /scratch/tmp after job end). it deletes directories in parallel. i checked logs: dozens of rm -rf processes spawn at once.

charlie: that rings alarm bells. parallel rm on nvme with small files = RANDOM tiny writes + metadata churn. For mitigation we did at another company: serialize deletes per node and add a rate limiter to the cleaner. Also drop concurrent delete workers from 64 -> 4.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-408 - nvme high io latency - us-west-2 (auto-detected by storage-alerts).

arya: other mitigations:
- set blkio.weight for the cleaner pod so it doesn't starve other processes
- reduce cleaner concurrency and add jitter between deletions
- switch node-level tmp cleanup to use systemd-tmpfiles with --remove-control-files (more serial)
- if on nodes with compression-enabled NVMe, try toggling compression to see if controller-side comp causes amplification

mike: +1 to blkio.cgroup. example (on containerd system):
```
# in pod spec: resources: 
  limits:
    io.kubernetes.io/blockIOWeight: "200"
```
or use cgroupv2 io.max for bytes per second.

lina: i've drained two worst nodes and set cleaner concurrency to 3. i'm also patching the cleaner to sleep 50-200ms between directory deletes. rolling change now.

charlie: long-term: we should add a preflight workload-test for deletion-heavy patterns to our node qualification suite (fio + find -delete mixed). Also add telemetry: histogram of unlink syscall rate per node.

arya: agree. i can add a quick eBPF probe to count unlink() per second and ship it to prometheus as node_unlink_rate. then we can alert when unlink_rate > 500/s for >5m.

mike: firmware note: some vendor nvme with inline compression + heavy metadata ops will exhibit worse latency under high metadata churn. we had a firmware patch in 2024 that improved it; check vendor release notes for this SKU.

lina: update: after reducing concurrency, p99 dropped from ~420ms to ~48ms and errors stopped for the last 12m on the drained nodes. leaving the patch rolling to rest of cluster.

charlie: nice. follow-ups:
- (lina) open PR to make cleaner concurrency configurable per-node-type
- (arya) add unlink eBPF metric and alert
- (mike) check vendor FW/SMART for the affected SKUs and file an RMA if SMART shows reallocated_sectors > threshold
- ops: consider a background serial scrub job for orphaned small files that is rate-limited

lina: on it. i'll post the PR link once up. thanks all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: INC-2026-408 acknowledged by eng-infra. assigned: lina.
